study_identification_part.si4_title: Normative trajectories of R 1 , R 2 *, and magnetic susceptibility in basal ganglia on healthy ageing

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To establish normative trajectories of qMRI parameters (R1, R2*, and magnetic susceptibility) and volume in subcortical grey matter nuclei across the adult lifespan (18-80 years), investigate the inter-dependencies of these metrics, and validate the models' utility in a clinical cohort (Parkinson's disease).

rci8_quality_checking.detail: Manual visual data curation was performed by three raters using the 'slicereport' tool. Data were excluded based on criteria including incomplete brain coverage, incorrect brain extraction, and visible motion artefacts (e.g., strong ringing). This process led to the exclusion of 41 out of 301 participants.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Two-sample t-tests were used to compare the z-scores and median qMRI values between healthy controls and Parkinson's disease patients. The Benjamini and Hochberg procedure was used for FDR correction at a level of 0.05.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: The study established age- and sex-specific normative trajectories for R1, R2*, and magnetic susceptibility in the basal ganglia, demonstrating that R1 follows a quadratic path while R2* and susceptibility are linear, and validated these models by detecting significant deviations in the substantia nigra of Parkinson's disease patients.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: This study established normative trajectories for R1, R2*, and magnetic susceptibility (χ) in the basal ganglia using a healthy cohort (N=260, aged 18-79). R1 trajectories showed an inverted U-shape, peaking around 45-60 years, whereas R2* and χ showed more linear increases with age. The models were validated on an independent cohort of healthy controls and Parkinson's disease (PD) patients. This validation reproduced known findings of significantly higher R2* and χ in the substantia nigra of PD patients compared to controls (adjusted p-values for SNc were 6.8e-7 for R2* and 1.5e-3 for χ). The study also demonstrated age-dependent changes in the spatial gradients of these metrics within the putamen and caudate nucleus.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: The authors state that the derived normative models may not be universally generalizable to other studies due to differences in MRI acquisition and processing pipelines. They also note the possibility of residual biases in R1 mapping despite B1 correction and acknowledge that pooling data from both hemispheres might mask subtle lateralized developmental effects.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: it is also  important  to  recognise  that  these  derived  models, even  within  the  realm  of  quantitative  imaging,  may  not hold universal validity across different studies...Despite our careful consideration of the B 1 effect...there  may  still  be  residual  biases...In this work, we pooled the subcortical nuclei from the left and right hemispheres together...However, the development/maturation between the left and right hemispheres may not be the  same...

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study highlights that using a large normative reference cohort (ABRIM, N=260) for comparison with the patient group significantly increased the statistical power to detect group differences, compared to using only the smaller, matched control group from the patient study (PPP, N=44). This demonstrates the practical utility of large-scale normative modeling for clinical research.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: The study makes its raw quantitative maps and derived metrics from the ABRIM healthy volunteer cohort publicly available to facilitate integration into future research. A key finding was that analyzing the thalamus as a single structure obscured distinct and sometimes opposing age-related trajectories in its sub-nuclei, emphasizing the importance of fine-grained anatomical analysis.
